findings.title: Revision-table append-only trigger name does not match the audit_events precedent it claims to mirror byte-for-byte
findings.problem: The design names the trigger academic_calendar_day_revisions_append_only and says it is 'identical in shape to audit_events_append_only'. In the live precedent (superadmin_security/migration.sql) the FUNCTION is audit_events_append_only and the TRIGGER is audit_events_no_update_delete. Reusing the function-style name for the trigger is cosmetic but makes the cited precedent hard to follow.
findings.fix: Name the function academic_calendar_day_revisions_append_only() and the trigger academic_calendar_day_revisions_no_update_delete (function + distinctly-named trigger, as the real precedent does); update §4.3/§8/§10.1 to the trigger name.

findings.title: requireModuleActive omission on the new student.ts reads is correct but not called out at the route, inviting implementation drift
findings.problem: Every existing route on apps/api/src/routes/student.ts pairs requirePermission with requireModuleActive('campus_movement') (verified). §5.5 correctly lists only requirePermission('academics.view') + withTenant per Decision A (academics is never module-gated), but does not explicitly flag that these routes must OMIT the requireModuleActive hook their peers carry. A coder mirroring the file could add it, wrongly gating the academics reads for every tenant (permanently, if keyed to academic_sessions which nothing activates).
findings.fix: Add one explicit sentence to §5.5: 'These routes carry NO requireModuleActive hook, unlike every peer route on student.ts, because academics is foundational, not a gated module (Decision A).' Add a code comment at the route.

findings.title: Soft-validation warnings response envelope shape is unspecified
findings.problem: The design introduces a non-fatal 'warnings' array (a new response convention not present in any live handler) and specifies when warnings are emitted but not the success-plus-warnings envelope shape or whether machine-readable codes accompany the human strings. Two callers (UI vs tests) could assume different shapes.
findings.fix: Pin the envelope in §5.1, e.g. '{ <resource>, warnings: Array<{ code: string; message: string }> }' with warnings=[] when none apply, and have §10.2 assert on warnings[].code.
